sentences.text:
---- Respondents
 (Cause title is taken from the Cis)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
For Appellant : Shri Ram Charan Sahu, Advocate on behalf of Shri Surfaraj Khan, Advocate For
Respondents/Claimants/1 to 5 : Shri Ashish Mittal, Advocate on behalf of Shri Ankit Singhal,
Advocate as Amicus Curiae For Respondent-6/Insurance Company : Shri Dashrath Gupta, Advocate
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Shri Justice Ravindra Kumar Agrawal Order on Board 15.02.2024
1.

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been preferred by NA2 (Non-Applicant 2), Owner of the offending vehicle- Truck (Dumper) against the award dated 27.01.2020, passed by the Mac 136 of 2021 learned First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mahasamund, District-Mahasamund in Claim Case-H-131/2018, whereby amount of Manoj Shukla vs Banshidhar Patel on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34561580/
1 compensation was awarded by the Tribunal in favour of the claimants/respondents-1 to 4 and the right to recovery of the compensation amount by the Insurance Company against the owner of offending was given by the impugned award, hence this appeal by the Owner of the offending vehicle.
2. Brief facts of the case are that on 14.02.2018, the wife of respondent-1, mother of respondent-2,
and grandmother of respondents- 3 and 4 were going to village-Rampur from their village-Golajhaar (Chandandipa) on Motorcycle (Hero Honda) bearing registration No.CG- 04-DJ-1709, being driven by respondent-1 (husband of the deceased).

When they reached near village-Singhupali (National Highway-53), husband of the deceased stopped his Motorcycle by seeing that the offending vehicle-Truck(Dumper) bearing registration No.CG-04-J-5015 coming from the opposite side very rashly and negligently, but it dashed the Motorcycle, by which, deceased-Lakshmi Patel received injuries and died on the spot.
The accident was reported to the Police Station-Pithora and after investigation, charge-sheet was filed against the NA1, Driver of the offending vehicle.
3. On account of death of deceased-Lakshmi Patel, aged about 49 years, Claimants filed a claim petition before the learned Claims Tribunal, claiming Rs.35,40,000/- towards compensation.

NA1 and 2 have jointly filed their written statement before the learned Claims Tribunal and pleaded that the owner and Insurance Company of the Motorcycle driven by claimant-1 has not been made party to the claim application in the present case and therefore, claim case suffered from non-joinder of necessary party.
Claimant-1 has not filed his Driving license and therefore, claimants are not entitled for any compensation amount.

5. NA3/Insurance Company has also filed its written statement in which Insurance Company denied the pleadings and has submitted that the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the Motorcycle by claimant-1.

The offending vehicle/ Truck (Dumper) was being driven by NA1 in violation of Policy conditions and the offending vehicle was not having any valid permit and fitness certificate on the date of accident, and therefore, there is violation of policy conditions and the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation.
6. On the basis of pleadings made by the parties, learned Claims Tribunal has framed six issues.
After appreciating the evidence available on record, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.5,38,000/- in favour of the Claimants as compensation.

However, the liability to pay compensation was ordered against the Owner of the vehicle ie NA2/ appellant herein, as the offending vehicle was not having any valid permit on the date of accident and right to recover the amount of compensation from the Owner was also granted in favour of the Insurance Company, in view of the decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court in cases of Manuara Khatun and others Vs Rajesh Kumar Singh and others with other (2017) Mac 136 of 2021 4SCC 796, and Amrit Paul Singh and another vs Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited and others (2018) 7 SCC 558.
7.

sentences.text: Present appeal is filed by the Owner of the offending vehicle against the liability part only.

Manoj Shukla vs Banshidhar Patel on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34561580/
2 8.

Learned counsel for the appellant/owner would submit that the Tribunal has erroneously passed the award by fastening the liability to pay compensation upon the owner of the offending vehicle though it was duly insured with the Insurance Company.

The vehicle was having valid permit earlier to the date of accident and also subsequent to the date, therefore, it cannot be said that the accident was occurred due to any mechanical fault or any reason, irrespective of availability or non- availability of the permit and therefore, the entire liability to pay compensation is upon the Insurance company.
9.

On the other hand, Shri Dashrath Gupta, learned counsel for the Insurance Company/respondent-6 supports the impugned award and would submit that permit of the 'Goods Vehicle' is the essential condition of the Insurance Policy, and if any goods vehicle is plying in absence of any valid permit, the same is in violation of the policy condition and thus, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation.
In the present case, the offending vehicle was not having any valid permit on the date of accident.

He would further submit that from the evidence of NA1 Rajesh Kumar Agrawal, Assistant Manager, who is the witness of the Insurance Company has duly approved the Insurance Policy, the report submitted by the Investigator proved that the offending vehicle was Mac 136 of 2021 not having any permit on the date of accident.
Therefore, the impugned award needs no interference.

10. This Court vide order dated 06.10.2023, requested Shri Ankit Singhal, Advocate to act as amicus curiae on behalf of respondents-1 to 4/claimants, as there was no representation on behalf of the claimants.

11. Shri Ashish Mittal, Advocate appears on behalf of Shri Ankit Singhal, learned counsel for respondents-1 to 4/claimants as amicus curiae, and submits that since the claimants have not filed any appeal against the amount awarded to them, it appears that they are satisfied with the amount of award and therefore, the same cannot be enhanced in absence of any appeal field by them.
12.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

13. Only issue raised by the appellant/owner of the offending vehicle in the present appeal is that,
whether, in absence of any valid permit on the date of accident, the liability can be imposed upon the Insurance Company or not.
The vehicle was duly insured with the Insurance Company and therefore, all the liability is upon the Insurance Company to satisfy the award.
However, he could not produce any document in his support that on the date of accident, there is valid permit in favour of the offending vehicle and there is no breach of any policy condition.

14. After detail examination of the evidence led by the parties, the Tribunal comes to the conclusion that there is no valid permit on the date of accident with respect to the offending vehicle and it was plying without Mac 136 of 2021 valid permit, which is in violation of policy condition and relying the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court in cases of Manuara Khatun (supra) and Amrit Paul (supra),
learned Tribunal has held that the Insurance Company is entitled to recover the amount of compensation from the owner/appellant herein, under the principles of 'Pay and recover'.

Manoj Shukla vs Banshidhar Patel on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34561580/
3 15.
In these facts and circumstances of the case, it cannot be said that the Tribunal has committed any error/mistake or the impugned award is unjustified.
16. In the result, the appellant is not able to produce any strong circumstance so as to interfere in the impugned award passed by the Claims Tribunal.
Consequently, the appeal fails and it is hereby dismissed.
17. No order as to cost.
18. This Court appreciates the assistance rendered by the Amicus Curiae in the case.

Sd/-
